output.summary: KEP-3895 added an interactive flag (--interactive / -i) to kubectl delete. It previews the resources to be deleted and asks the user to confirm with y before deleting. The KEP is marked implemented and stable.
output.rationale: Deletes are irreversible and mistakes (mistyping, hasty tab completion) are easy to make. Making confirmation the default would break backwards compatibility, so the KEP adds an opt-in flag to ask for confirmation before deleting. Deletion is limited to the UIDs shown in the preview, so resources that changed after the preview are not removed.

alternatives.option: Make confirmation the default behavior of kubectl delete
alternatives.why_not: Due to the backwards compatibility concerns, seeking confirmation from a user before proceeding to genuinely delete as default, is out of the table.

alternatives.option: Use a --interactive=never|once|always style option, as rm does
alternatives.why_not: Proposed by atiratree in review as an alternative; the sources do not say it was adopted. Reviewer ardaguclu noted it was 'not sure how feasible/hacky it is to do with cobra'.
Listed as a non-goal. Reviewer soltysh suggested a ValidatingAdmissionWebhook for server-side protection instead.

evidence.quote: Due to the backwards compatibility concerns, seeking confirmation from a user before proceeding to genuinely delete as default, is out of the table.
The system is moving constantly, we should be operating on the view that was created during the first invocation and to which user explicitly agreed to.
I think, we can close this issue as completed as it has been promoted to stable in 1.30.
after removal of this environment variable, `interactive` flag can be used directly and will be enabled by default.
